prompt_text: overhead editorial photograph of a physical artifact-sorting rig on a steel workbench, where prior-project materials move through three bounded sorting lanes: reusable structure, refresh-required assets, and retire-only snapshots; the explanatory logic should come from trays, clips, and material differences rather than labels, colors-as-legends, or infographic tables. no readable text, no labels, no numbers, no dashboard UI, no chart board look, no generic slide layout, no decorative software schematic. Target aspect ratio: 16:9 Critical render rule: do not generate any readable text, letters, numbers, captions, labels, logos, watermarks, slide titles, document copy, dashboard copy, UI text, headline text, wall text, or typographic overlays anywhere in the image. If a screen, board, document, dashboard, scorecard, or interface is visible, it must contain only abstract non-readable blocks, simple shapes, and soft placeholder marks. Never place large title words, marketing slogans, section headers, or composited text for later overlay; leave that area visually quiet and empty instead. Use unlabeled structure, simple shapes, tokens, lanes, connectors, and status cues instead of screenshot-like dashboards or reports. Analytical image rule: avoid screenshot aesthetics, whiteboard snapshots, slide decks, tables with headers, and infographic panels with text. Prefer a premium enterprise visual metaphor built from cards, modules, flows, physical markers, subtle charts without labels, and clean operational structure. Do not label stages directly inside the image; represent system stages through position, grouping, material contrast, and abstract markers only.
negative_prompt: generic recycling symbol cliche, spreadsheet table, whiteboard matrix, readable labels, software asset catalog.
alt_text_en: visualize how a buyer should sort previous project artifacts into reuse, refresh, and retire decisions without turning it into a slide.
caption_en: visualize how a buyer should sort previous project artifacts into reuse, refresh, and retire decisions without turning it into a slide.
